text:
Aisha: quick proposal — add an `x-model-preference` header + route-level pinning that respects a compatibility matrix. thinking: route config can pin alias, or set pin="prefer"/"require" and a fallback chain. want feedback before I draft the migration plan.

Marco: :eyes: can you sketch the precedence rules? e.g. request header vs route pin vs default alias?

Aisha: precedence idea: 1) route forced pin (highest), 2) request-level header if allowed by route policy, 3) user/tenant default, 4) route default alias. fallback chain applied only if pin is not "require".

Priya: how does billing/quotas work with fallbacks? if user requests a pinned model but falls back to cheaper variant, what gets billed/attributed?

Sam: telemetry must record resolved_model and pin_reason. billing should charge actual runtime model tokens. attribution can link to original route/header for quota accounting.

Lena: console UX: show resolved_model in request inspector, and a rollout tab that displays "alias -> versions" with percentages and compatibility health. Also need a way to preview which model a sample request would hit given headers.

Jonah: compatibility concerns: some clients pin to fp16 numeric-only models; if we fallback to quantized variant with slightly different logits we risk hallucination regressions. suggest adding a compatibility level in catalog: `compatible`, `approx`, `incompatible`. router should refuse fallbacks when compatibility == `incompatible` and pin is "require".

Aisha: yes — adding `compatibility_level` to model metadata is good. also thinking of quick rule snippet:
```
route: /chat/*
match: host=acme
model_selection:
  alias: chat-x
  pin_strategy: prefer  # prefer | require | ignore
  allowed_compat: [compatible, approx]
  fallback: [chat-x-quant, chat-x-small]
```

Marco: for implementation, keep the runtime decision deterministic and idempotent. we should compute resolved_model at the gateway, sign it into trace/span and passthrough header `x-resolved-model`. runtime nodes then validate compatibility and reject if mismatch.

Priya: rollout UX question — can we do gradual version pinning? like roll out chat-x-v2 to 10% of requests but only for routes that opted in. Need an easy console slider.

Lena: yes — we can surface a "route rollout" control that writes a rollout config and a policy that the router uses to sample. sampling keys: route+tenant+user for sticky behavior.

Sam: alerting: add detection for spike in error-rate or latency when fallback engages. also track cost delta when fallback chosen vs requested model.

Jonah: small implementation nit: when request header requests an alias that isn't allowed by route policy, respond with 403 or ignore? leaning towards 403 with body hint to use `?pin=prefer` or contact owner. easier to debug.

Aisha: agree on 403 for explicit require/denied headers. For silent prefer, we just log and continue.

Marco: one more — compatibility checks must be efficient. keep a precomputed compatibility vector per alias pair (bitset). runtime does quick lookup. update when models onboarded.

Priya: can we add an "evaluation set" check during rollout to auto-promote or rollback if quality drops? product likes auto-guardrails.

Aisha: add to roadmap: rollout eval + auto-rollback. DevEx can provide prompt sets.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary: model-router-service v2 -> canary on eng-platform (5% traffic) at 2026-03-22T09:00Z :rocket:

Lena: action items: Aisha will PR route schema + migration proposal, Marco will prototype `x-resolved-model` header, Jonah will draft compatibility vector format, Priya will define rollout UX mockups, Sam will list telemetry signals.

Aisha: thanks all, I'll drop a short RFC and link to the console mockups. :thumbsup:
